items.title: Fed survey shows continued economic growth, sticky inflation in recent weeks By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 25 (Reuters) - Economic growth persisted at a "slight to moderate" pace across most of the US in recent weeks, while inflation remained sticky and employment levels rose, a Federal Reserve survey showed on Wednesday, two weeks before central bank policymakers decide whether to raise interest rates. "Prices increased moderately overall, as in the prior reporting period," the Fed said in its latest "Beige Book" report, a compendium of survey-based data and commentary from businesses compiled by its 12 regional banks to provide a read on economic conditions. "Contacts across a range of sectors reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, health care, insurance, and tariff-related expenses." Still, input costs were outpacing selling price increases, suggesting growing pressure on corporate margins, the report said. "(C)ompetitive pressures and customer price sensitivity limited firms’ ability to fully pass through higher costs. Contacts expected both expenses and prices to continue rising in the coming months." ... The overall picture across the country was varied, with eight districts reporting growth and four reporting that activity was unchanged. Business investment — led by the artificial intelligence boom — remained strong, but consumer spending was flat as households were increasingly stretched and trading down.

items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: EMBARGOED UNTIL RELEASE AT 8:30 a.m. EST, Wednesday, November 25, 2026 # GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated.

items.title: For Trump, doubling down on tariffs is about power, not popularity - World - DAWN.COM
items.excerpt: The Trump administration on Wednesday announced a new round of tariffs on goods from 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union, a seemingly counterintuitive move that reflects both Trump’s decades-old belief in tariffs and a new political reality confronting his White House. With Democrats set to control Congress for the final two years of his presidency, tariffs are taking on added importance as one of the most potent economic tools Trump can wield without lawmakers’ approval. Tariffs are taxes levied on imports, raising costs for consumers. But Trump sees them as a way to wring concessions from foreign leaders, force corporate CEOs to build plants in the US, raise cash for the government and curry favour with blue-collar voters, according to US officials and other people familiar with the president’s thinking. And after a midterm defeat for his party that threatens to sharply constrain his domestic agenda, Trump is eager to demonstrate that he remains capable of driving economic policy and exercising power even as his legislative clout diminishes, the people said.

items.title: Congress Faces Busy Lame-Duck Session - Federal Caucus Post
items.excerpt: Lawmakers have returned to Capitol Hill this week following the midterm elections. Republicans face a packed agenda before Democrats assume control in January. ... Federal funding is set to expire on December 11. Without a new agreement, there could be another government shutdown. Some Democrats, according to POLITICO, may use President Donald Trump’s actions in Iran as a bargaining chip in spending negotiations. This tactic might lead to financial hurdles that could disrupt federal operations. A House Republican, speaking anonymously, anticipated another short-term extension of current funding levels, known as a continuing resolution (CR), extending into February or March of next year. The existing CR covers until the end of November, following the end of the fiscal year on September 30. Senate Majority Leader John Thune and House Speaker Mike Johnson will navigate a busy period before the party transition. “No one wants a shutdown,” a House Republican stated. “Not even Democrats.” Other legislative priorities include the farm bill, which establishes the country’s food and agriculture policy every five years. Republicans are also aiming to pass a transportation infrastructure bill and a bipartisan tax package by year’s end. The debt ceiling deadline looms in January, and Trump is likely to urge Republicans to address it.

items.excerpt: NEW YORK (AP) — Organizers have postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade for the first time ever because powerful winds are expected during the time when marchers and spectators would have been on New York City's streets. Macy's said Wednesday the parade will be held Saturday, citing discussions with the city and safety concerns. Emergency management officials and weather forecasters say gusts up to 60 mph and heavy rainfall are expected in the city Thursday. NBC will broadcast a rerun of the 2025 parade Thursday in place of the live event. The rescheduled parade will kick off at 8:30 a.m. Saturday. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016, alleging Pitt abused her and their children during a flight. The FBI investigated but didn't pursue charges.
